Around.summary: A number with an uncertainty, propagated to first order through arithmetic and functions.

examples.caption: A power scales the uncertainty by the derivative, $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 0.1$
An exact factor scales the uncertainty
Through a special function, with its derivative as slope

Association.summary: A keyed collection of rules key -> value; compute-engine's Dictionary is the nearest head, and the list heads would need to accept it.

examples.caption: [[First]] is the first value, not the first rule
[[Join]] merges keys; a later value for a repeated key wins, in the key's original position

BellY.summary: The partial Bell polynomial B_{n,k}(x_1, x_2, ...).

examples.caption: $x_j = j!$ gives the Lah number L(4, 2)

CarmichaelLambda.summary: The Carmichael function: the exponent of the multiplicative group mod n. compute-engine has it, undocumented here; these are the gaps.

CenteredInterval.summary: A ball c ± r with rigorous (outward-rounded) arithmetic; the complex-capable sibling of Interval.

examples.caption: An exact factor scales center and radius

ComplexExpand.summary: Expand an expression into real and imaginary parts, assuming the variables are real.

examples.caption: $\sin(x + iy) = \sin x\cosh y + i\cos x\sinh y$
Polar form of a complex exponential
Wolfram leaves $e^{i\pi/5}$ alone until asked; this is the radical form compute-engine's Exp already produces

ContinuedFractionK.summary: The continued fraction f_1/(g_1 + f_2/(g_2 + ...)) over an index range, finite or infinite.

Convergents.summary: The successive convergents p_k/q_k of a continued fraction, given as its list of terms or as the number itself.

examples.caption: A rational: the last convergent is the number itself

DivisorSum.summary: The sum of f(d) over the positive divisors d of n, optionally only those satisfying a condition.

EulerE.summary: The Euler numbers $E_n$ and Euler polynomials $E_n(x)$.

ExpToTrig.summary: Rewrite exponentials as circular and hyperbolic functions -- the inverse of TrigToExp.

examples.caption: A real exponential splits into hyperbolic parts

FixedPoint.summary: Iterates f from x until the result no longer changes.

examples.caption: Halving and flooring until nothing changes
The Dottie number, the fixed point of cos
Newton's method for $\sqrt{2}$, run to machine precision

FrobeniusNumber.summary: The largest integer that is not a non-negative integer combination of the given positive integers.

examples.caption: Not coprime: infinitely many numbers are unreachable

FrobeniusSolve.summary: All non-negative integer solutions x of a·x = b, lexicographically.

examples.caption: 43 is the Frobenius number of $\{6,9,20\}$, so it has no solutions

FullSimplify.summary: Simplify harder, trying a wider set of transformations including special-function identities.

FunctionExpand.summary: Rewrites special functions in terms of more elementary or better-known ones.

examples.caption: Radicals past the automatic special-angle table
A rising factorial with an integer length becomes a polynomial

Gather.summary: Group identical elements into sublists, in order of first appearance.

examples.caption: A test decides which elements belong together: here, same parity
The group sizes are the multiplicities of the distinct elements

GatherBy.summary: Group elements by the value of a function, in order of first appearance.

examples.caption: Pairs grouped by their last element

GeometricMean.summary: The n-th root of the product of n values.

HarmonicMean.summary: The reciprocal of the mean of the reciprocals.

examples.caption: Driving equal distances at 40 and 60 averages 48, not 50
Equal values are their own harmonic mean

Hyperfactorial.summary: The hyperfactorial H(n) = prod_{k=1}^n k^k, continued to complex arguments; Gamma(n+1)^n / BarnesG(n+1).

HypergeometricPFQ.summary: The generalized hypergeometric function ${}_pF_q(a; b; z)$.

IntegerLength.summary: The number of digits of n in the given base (default 10).

IntegerReverse.summary: The integer whose digits are those of n in reverse order.

examples.caption: trailing zeros become leading zeros and vanish
a palindrome is its own reversal

Interval.summary: Interval arithmetic: compute-engine declares Interval(a, b) as a real set, but arithmetic and functions do not yet map intervals to intervals.

examples.caption: A product takes the extreme endpoint products
Reciprocal of an interval not containing 0
An even power of an interval straddling 0 starts at 0, not at 1
The dependency problem: interval arithmetic doesn't know both operands are the same quantity
The absolute value of an interval straddling 0

InverseBetaRegularized.summary: The inverse of the regularized incomplete beta $I_x(a, b)$ in $x$: the Beta-distribution quantile.

examples.caption: $I_x(2, 1) = x^2$, so the inverse at $1/4$ is $1/2$

InverseErfc.summary: The inverse complementary error function: solves $\operatorname{erfc}(y) = s$ for $0 < s < 2$.

examples.caption: $\sqrt2$ times this, $2.5758\ldots$, is the two-sided 99% normal critical value
Deep in the tail it keeps full precision, where $\operatorname{erf}^{-1}(1 - s)$ would lose it

InverseGammaRegularized.summary: The inverse of the regularized incomplete gamma $Q(a, z)$ in $z$: solves $s = Q(a, z)$.

examples.caption: $Q(1, z) = e^{-z}$, so the inverse at $1/2$ is $\ln 2$
The median of the Gamma(2, 1) distribution

IsCoprime.summary: Tests whether integers are pairwise relatively prime.

examples.caption: Several arguments: every pair must be coprime
Pairwise, not collectively: $\gcd(6,10,15)=1$ yet no pair is coprime
Gaussian integers: $2+i$ and $2-i$ are non-associate primes

IsPerfect.summary: Tests whether n equals the sum of its proper divisors. compute-engine has it, undocumented here; these are the gaps.

IsPrimePower.summary: Tests whether n is a positive power of a single prime.

examples.caption: A prime is its own first power

IsQuadraticIrrational.summary: True when x is an irrational root of a quadratic with integer coefficients — exactly the numbers with an eventually periodic continued fraction.

examples.caption: A cube root is algebraic of degree 3

Khinchin.summary: Khinchin's constant $K_0 = 2.68545\ldots$, the almost-sure geometric mean of continued-fraction terms.

KleinInvariantJ.summary: Klein's absolute invariant J(tau) = j(tau)/1728, normalised so J(i) = 1 and J(e^{2 pi i/3}) = 0. We have ModularJ (unnormalised j) already.

LambertW.summary: compute-engine declares LambertW (Wolfram's ProductLog), the inverse of $w e^w$, but only evaluates it numerically; exact values, the $k$-th branch and a Wolfram mapping are missing.

LinearRecurrence.summary: The sequence of a linear recurrence with constant coefficients, from its kernel and initial values.

examples.caption: the Lucas numbers: same kernel, other initial values

MangoldtLambda.summary: The von Mangoldt function: $\ln p$ if n is a power of the prime p, else 0.

MatrixFunction.summary: A scalar function f extended to a square matrix M via its power series or eigendecomposition.

examples.caption: The principal square root of a diagonal matrix
On a diagonal matrix, f acts on the diagonal
A polynomial f agrees with the matrix power

MersennePrimeExponent.summary: The exponent p of the nth Mersenne prime $2^p-1$.

Nest.summary: f applied n times to x.

NestList.summary: The list of x, f(x), f(f(x)), ... up to n applications of f.

examples.caption: 3 is a primitive root mod 7: its powers visit every nonzero residue

NoneTrue.summary: Whether no element of a collection satisfies a predicate.

examples.caption: Vacuously true on an empty list

NorlundB.summary: The Nörlund polynomial B_n^(a), from the generating function (t/(e^t - 1))^a.

examples.caption: At a = 1 it is the Bernoulli number $B_2$

NumberExpand.summary: The place-value terms of n: each digit times its power of the base.

Outer.summary: The generalized outer product: f applied to every pair drawn from two lists.

examples.caption: The outer product of two vectors, a $3 \times 2$ matrix
Any binary function: an addition table
$List$ gives every pair, like a Cartesian product

PadLeft.summary: Pad a list on the left to length n (with 0 or a given element), or truncate it from the left.

examples.caption: Padded with zeros on the left
A shorter length drops elements from the left
With no length, a ragged array is padded to a full matrix

PadRight.summary: Pad a list on the right to length n (with 0 or a given element), or truncate it from the right.

examples.caption: Padded with zeros on the right
A shorter length drops elements from the right
With no length, a ragged array is padded to a full matrix

PartitionsQ.summary: The number q(n) of partitions of n into distinct parts.

examples.caption: The partitions of 10 into distinct parts
Euler: as many partitions into odd parts as into distinct parts

PowerExpand.summary: Expand powers and logarithms of products as if every variable were positive.

examples.caption: Splits a logarithm of a product
Distributes a power over a product

PowersRepresentations.summary: The ways to write n as a sum of k non-negative p-th powers, as non-decreasing lists.

examples.caption: The smallest number that is a sum of two positive squares in two ways
A polynomial in q whose coefficients count partitions in a 2 × 2 box
At q = 1 it is the ordinary factorial
The inversion generating function of SymmetricGroup(3): $\sum_\pi q^{inv(\pi)}$

QPochhammer.summary: The q-Pochhammer symbol (a; q)_n = (1 - a)(1 - a q)...(1 - a q^(n-1)).

examples.caption: The infinite product, Euler's function at 1/2

RamanujanTau.summary: Ramanujan's tau function: the coefficients of the discriminant modular form q prod (1 - q^n)^24.

RealDigits.summary: The digits of a real number and the position of its decimal point, with the repeating block of a rational marked as a sublist.

examples.caption: the first 10 digits of $\pi$ (truncated, not rounded)
an integer: six digits before the point

RecurrenceTable.summary: A table of the values of a sequence defined by a recurrence equation and initial conditions.

RiemannSiegelZ.summary: The Riemann–Siegel function $Z(t) = e^{i\vartheta(t)}\zeta(\tfrac12 + it)$, real for real $t$.

RiemannZetaZero.summary: The k-th nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line (compute-engine's Fungrim identity table already spells it `RiemannZetaZero`).

Riffle.summary: Interleave a separator (or a second list) between the elements of a list.

examples.caption: Interleave two lists of the same length
A list one shorter goes strictly between the elements
Every 3rd element of the result is x
A single element has nothing to separate

RomanNumeral.summary: The Roman numeral for a non-negative integer, as a string.

examples.caption: zero is written N, for nulla

SortBy.summary: The collection sorted by the value of a function on each element.

examples.caption: Pairs sorted by their last element
Sorted by the square of each element

Span.summary: A range of positions i;;j;;step used as a part specification, with negative positions counted from the end.

examples.caption: Every other element through the last ($1;;-1;;2$)
Negative bounds: the last two elements
Spans at two levels cut out a submatrix

Split.summary: Split a list into runs of identical adjacent elements.

examples.caption: Runs, not groups: the two runs of 1 stay apart
A test between neighbours: split into increasing runs

SplitBy.summary: Split a list into runs on which a function is constant.

examples.caption: Runs with the same value of $\lfloor x/4 \rfloor$

SquaresR.summary: The number of ways to write n as a sum of d squares, counting signs and order.

examples.caption: No $n\equiv3\pmod4$ is a sum of two squares

UpTo.summary: A count specification meaning at most n, taking fewer when fewer are available.

examples.caption: Asking for up to 5 of 3 elements takes all 3, with no error
When enough elements are available, exactly n are taken
In [[Partition]], a shorter final chunk is allowed
In [[Ordering]], at most 6 positions of a 5-element list
